primary_claim: Today's general-purpose agentic systems (AutoGPT, AgentGPT, NinjaTech AI) do not surpass frontier chat LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-o1 preview) on GAIA-benchmark capability questions, and show fewer safety guardrails than those chat LLMs on METR-inspired risk-relevant tasks.

effect.metric: GAIA benchmark accuracy, all levels combined (%)
effect.value: GPT-4o 26%, GPT-o1 preview 40%, AutoGPT 5.1 16%, AgentGPT 9%, NinjaTech AI 16%

contradicts_or_qualifies: Mialon et al. (2023) described AutoGPT4's GAIA performance as 'disappointing' (0% Level 3, 0.4% Level 2, 14% Level 1); this project's AutoGPT 5.1 shows improved scores (8%, 19%, 16%) though still below the GPT-4o/GPT-o1 controls
stated_future_work: Investigating the extent to which a misaligned agent could decompose a malign task into apparently-benign subtasks, such that LLMs and other API-accessible systems fed those subtasks would provide an 'unwittingly' helpful response
Investigating the ways in which different agentic architectures affect both capability and safety, given the same base LLM
Investigating the difference in the safety/alignment of responses from agentic systems when paired with LLMs whose developers employ different approaches to aligning their models
limitations_stated: Many GAIA questions require file upload, which not all agentic systems supported to the same degree, so the 165 public questions were refined down to 80
AgentGPT hit its maximum loop count before completing responses, so a full set of 80 responses could not be obtained for it
All helpfulness/harmlessness rankings are necessarily somewhat subjective, based on author discretion
With the very small sample of questions tested against AgentGPT, it is not possible to make generalisations or identify trends with any significant confidence
This project only scratched the surface of investigating the extent to which agentic systems justify the hype around their capabilities and risks
quote: Results indicate that today's general-purpose agentic systems do not yet surpass frontier LLMs in general capabilities but do exhibit some promise in complex tasks.
